claim: For the scalar benchmark \(f(x)=\sqrt{1+x^2}-x\cos x\) used in arXiv:2607.10741v1, the least \(L_0\) such that \(|f'''(x)|\le L_0+|f'(x)|\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R\) is exactly \(L_0=3\). Equivalently, at the source's natural choice \(L_1=1\), the pointwise generalized-smoothness certificate improves sharply from the printed pair \((6,1)\) to \((3,1)\). This value is optimal because along \(x_n=2\pi n\), \(|f'''(x_n)|-|f'(x_n)|\to3\).
integrity: The proof is analytic: an exact polynomial identity proves the global upper bound and an explicit sequence proves optimality. The bundled computation is a consistency replay only. The primary source was inspected directly and residual literature risk is disclosed.
scientific_limitations: The theorem classifies only the fixed-slope slice L1=1 of the pointwise generalized-smoothness condition for the single scalar benchmark. It does not determine the full (L0,L1) Pareto frontier, prove a complexity lower bound, or extend automatically to other objectives.
title: Sharp generalized-smoothness intercept for a 2026 cubic-Newton benchmark
